legend: Valera has a strip infinite in both directions and consisting of cells. The cells are numbered by integers. The cell number 0 has a robot.

The robot has instructions — the sequence of moves that he must perform. In one move, the robot moves one cell to the left or one cell to the right, according to instructions. Before the robot starts moving, Valera puts obstacles in some cells of the strip, excluding cell number 0. If the robot should go into the cell with an obstacle according the instructions, it will skip this move.

Also Valera indicates the finish cell in which the robot has to be after completing the entire instructions. The finishing cell should be different from the starting one. It is believed that the robot completed the instructions successfully, if during the process of moving he visited the finish cell exactly once — at its last move. Moreover, the latter move cannot be skipped.

Let's assume that k is the minimum number of obstacles that Valera must put to make the robot able to complete the entire sequence of instructions successfully and end up in some finishing cell. You need to calculate in how many ways Valera can choose k obstacles and the finishing cell so that the robot is able to complete the instructions successfully.
input: The first line contains a sequence of characters without spaces s1s2... sn (1 ≤ n ≤ 106), consisting only of letters "L" and "R". If character si equals "L", then the robot on the i-th move must try to move one cell to the left. If the si-th character equals "R", then the robot on the i-th move must try to move one cell to the right.
output: Print a single integer — the required number of ways. It's guaranteed that this number fits into 64-bit signed integer type.
note: In the first sample Valera mustn't add any obstacles and his finishing cell must be cell 2.

In the second sample, Valera must add an obstacle in cell number 1, and his finishing cell must be cell number  - 1. In this case robot skips the first two moves and on the third move he goes straight from the starting cell to the finishing one. But if Valera doesn't add any obstacles, or adds an obstacle to another cell, then the robot visits the finishing cell more than once.

legend.ai: Valera 有一条向两个方向无限延伸、由格子组成的条带。格子用整数编号。编号为 0 的格子中有一个机器人。
机器人拥有一些指令——也就是它必须执行的移动序列。每次移动时，机器人会根据指令向左移动一个单元格或向右移动一个单元格。在机器人开始移动之前，Valera 会在条带上的一些单元格中放置障碍物，但不包括编号为 0 的单元格。如果根据指令机器人应该进入一个有障碍物的单元格，那么它会跳过这次移动。
此外，Valera 还指定了终点单元格，机器人执行完全部指令后必须位于该单元格中。终点单元格必须与起始单元格不同。如果机器人在移动过程中恰好访问终点单元格一次，并且是在最后一次移动时访问的，那么就认为它成功完成了这些指令。此外，最后一次移动不能被跳过。
设 k 是 Valera 必须放置的最少障碍物数量，使机器人能够成功完成整个指令序列并最终到达某个终点单元格。你需要计算 Valera 选择这 k 个障碍物和终点单元格，使机器人能够成功完成这些指令的方案数。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个不含空格的字符序列 s1s2... sn（1 ≤ n ≤ 106），仅由字母“L”和“R”组成。如果字符 si 等于“L”，那么机器人在第 i 次移动时必须尝试向左移动一个单元格。如果第 i 个字符等于“R”，那么机器人在第 i 次移动时必须尝试向右移动一个单元格。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——所求的方案数。保证该数可以用 64 位有符号整数类型表示。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Valera 不需要添加任何障碍物，且终点单元格必须是编号为 2 的单元格。
在第二个样例中，Valera 必须在编号为 1 的格子中添加一个障碍物，并且终点格必须是编号为 -1 的格子。在这种情况下，机器人会跳过前两步，并在第三步时从起点直接前往终点。但如果 Valera 不添加任何障碍物，或将障碍物添加到其他格子中，那么机器人会多次经过终点格。
